$CWST is a $6.2B waste company that gained 16.8% in 21 sessions while the S&P 500 lost 5.0%. My Golden Cross screener flagged it, and I want to own it. I will pay less than the $98.21 close of November 6.

The market sees a garbage contract that still pays in a downturn, and it bid the stock up while everything else fell. The market ignores the price tag. $CWST trades at 66.2x forward earnings with a profitability score of 15/100, so the entry matters more than the story.

The Setup

Casella collects, sorts and buries trash and recyclables across the US Northeast. It owns the landfills, the transfer stations and the trucks, and towns pay it under long contracts. Revenue grew 17% last quarter against the same quarter a year earlier. Part of that growth comes from buying regional haulers, which is how this company grows. Earnings are thin today: $0.09 a share over twelve months, far below what the Street expects next year. That gap makes the trailing P/E 1048.9x and the forward one 66.2x, and the stock trades at 3.96x book value. Industrials are where money went this month, and waste is the most defensive corner of the sector. This is a defensive grower priced for perfection, and I only want it on a dip.

The stock topped at $107.96 on February 11, then lost almost a third of its value into the $74.05 low on March 25. Since then it has climbed back steadily. The last month did most of the work: +16.8% for $CWST against -5.0% for the S&P 500. It closed November 6 at $98.21 (-1.9% on the session), 71% of the 52-week range between $74.05 and $107.96.

I read this chart through volume. After a run of 16.8% in a month, the only prices that hold are the ones where shares changed hands. The close at $98.21 sits right on support at $98.03, with 0% of cushion. Above it, $100.06 is the supply left over from the 3-month high, and $101.16 is the next resistance. That leaves about two dollars of room before sellers show up. The February high at $107.96 is the real ceiling, which means everyone who bought the top is still about 9% underwater and will sell into any rally that gets close. Under the price, $92.22 is the level where I expect buyers to defend the pullback, and a daily close under $84.23 ends the structure. I would not buy support at $98.03 with two dollars of upside above it. I would let it come back toward $92.22 and scale in there. If it pays at $100.06, take the win and do not wait for the February high.

Fundamentals

Score: 33/100

The Good: revenue grew 17% last quarter against the same quarter a year earlier, and the risk and dilution pillar is the strongest of the five at 50/100. Free cash flow is disputed. Yahoo shows $121.70M of free cash flow, and the app's read of the SEC filings flags a burn. I will wait for the next report before I count on that cash.

The Bad: the profitability pillar sits at 15/100, valuation at 37/100, growth at 34/100 and the balance sheet at 34/100. 11% of the float is sold short, which is heavy for a utility-like business. At 1048.9x trailing earnings, the stock prices next year's earnings in already.

The Street is bullish: 10 analysts cover it, consensus buy, average target $106.50, 8.4% above the last close. The low target is $91.00 and the high is $130.00. The 33 hides a split. Analysts like a steady contract business, and the income statement does not yet support the price.

The Sector

$CWST sits in industrials, and the industrials bench is widening. 44.6% of the S&P 500 industrial names trade above their trend, and that share is growing. The participation is mid-range, so the sector has room to run before it gets crowded. I prefer to buy a leader in a sector that is broadening.

Confluence

The Golden Cross screener flagged $CWST because the longer trend has started to turn after the spring low. The turn is incomplete. The trend has not confirmed yet, so this is an early entry into a new uptrend, and the risk is that it stalls.

The relative strength explains why the screener caught it now. A stock that beats the S&P by 22.8% in a month during a selloff tells me buyers are using it as a place to hide. The funds confirm part of that. In the last quarterly filings, 5 funds raised their position and 3 cut it. Baron Capital's line rose 64.2% in value to $93.60M, and Fisher, AQR and Two Sigma also added. Marshall Wace cut its line 59.2% and Caxton exited. These are changes in value, so part of the increase is the stock price itself.

The long-only holder with the biggest line added, and the fast quant money is split. That makes this a slow accumulation trade. It is not a squeeze. You buy the dip and you give it weeks.

Options Flow

The options money is small, and it leans one way. On November 4, calls took $18K of premium against $3K for puts, 85% on the call side. The cleanest read among the near expirations is the December 18 $105 call: open interest rose by 20 contracts to 68, so the buyers held the position overnight. That strike is also where dealers carry their biggest call position, and their biggest put position sits at $90. Implied volatility is 43.6%. The flow is too thin to lead the trade, and it points at the same ceiling I see on the chart.

How To Play It

Conservative:

Entry: $92.22 to $98.03 (current pullback zone)

Stop: $84.23 (a daily close under it breaks the setup)

Target 1: $100.06 (the supply near the 3-month high)

Target 2: $107.96 (the 52-week high)

From $92.22, you risk 8.7% to make 8.5% to Target 1, about one for one. That ratio is why I scale in on the way down and keep it at half size, capped around 3% of the account.

Aggressive:

Buy a starter at $98.21, on the $98.03 support, with the same stop and the same targets. The math is bad: you risk the whole drop to $84.23 to make the short move to $100.06. This only works if the relative strength keeps going and the stock runs through $100.06 toward $107.96 without a pullback. Keep the starter to a quarter of the position and add the rest at $92.22.

What Could Go Wrong

A waste company at 66.2x forward earnings has no room for a soft quarter, and one guidance cut reprices it fast. 11% of the float is short, so a break of $92.22 can speed up on the way down. The trend has not confirmed yet, and the stock rallied while the S&P fell 5.0%, so a rotation out of defensives would hit it first. Half size, 3% max.

Size accordingly.
